data.title: bn-1nmq: CML parser nesting bound counts postfix chains and real tree depth; fuzz harness and pipeline laws

data.body:
[HIGH][CWE-674] The type-depth oracle skips a parser path that reattaches parsed subtrees.

Evidence: parser.rs:788-794 parses the function left side at the current depth. It then places that subtree below a new Function node. Define T0 as Nat and Tn as Set[Tn-1] -> Nat. T63 reaches parser depth 64, but its returned AST depth is 127. The parser therefore accepts it at MAX_NESTING. This file skips all type trees and states the opposite assumption. The TooDeep oracle cannot detect this shape. Recursive consumers include dump.rs:207-218, print.rs:227-260, and elab.rs:445-492.

Failure modes: hostile CML can exceed the promised tree bound and exhaust stack in later recursive passes.

Edge cases: nested applied types with a function root accumulate one hidden level per wrapper. Ordinary applied-only and right-hand function chains do not expose the same gap.

Rollback: revert the depth-evidence claim if a production fix cannot land in this range. Keep the review blocked until the evidence is honest.

Monitoring: add iterative type-depth measurement before dump, print, elaboration, or Drop-sensitive work. Treat any accepted depth above MAX_NESTING as a typed defect.

Validation: add T62, T63, and T64 boundary cases on the 1 MiB probe stack. Assert acceptance never returns a type tree above MAX_NESTING. Arm the oracle with a type-depth mutant or the vulnerable parser.

Required fix: account for the left-subtree shift in ty_inner and extend the iterative depth oracle to every TypeExpr root.

data.reason: HIGH: function-type left subtrees can bypass MAX_NESTING and reach depth 127, while the new oracle skips all type trees. See th-qospz9.

data.body: [HIGH][RESOLVED] Target d2672c3 fixes the type-tree reattachment gap. parser.rs:796-821 measures the left subtree, charges the new Function root before parsing the right child, and refuses above MAX_NESTING. depth.rs:55-134 now walks every expression and type root iteratively. errors.rs:627-665 and cml_fuzz.rs:605-656 pin the accepted and refused boundaries. Static review found no remaining path that returns a type tree above the bound.

data.reason: Fixed at d2672c3 and verified across parser accounting, iterative depth measurement, and boundary cases.

data.body: [risk:high][NO FINDINGS] Whole-range security assessment for 40e9dd16..d2672c3d. Failure modes: hostile CML could previously create left-deep expression, postfix, or function-type trees beyond MAX_NESTING and exhaust stack in dump, print, elaboration, or Drop. The range now rejects each reattachment before it passes the bound. Edge cases: reviewed left and right associativity, mixed precedence, postfix arguments and keys, parenthesized groups, applied and record types, left and right function chains, sibling roots, and T31/T32/T62-T64 boundaries. Rollback: do not roll back to 40e9dd16 while untrusted CML remains enabled because that base retains the known deep-tree paths. If this target regresses, stop promotion and disable untrusted CML ingestion until a bounded replacement is reviewed. Monitoring: keep cml.limit.nesting_too_deep visible, and treat Panicked, Hung, TooDeep, process abort, or campaign landing drift as a release blocker. Validation: static review covered all 81 changed files and all three commits. parser.rs:384-397, 780-821, 920-1051, and 1171-1202 enforce the bound. depth.rs:55-173 measures every AST tree iteratively. errors.rs:446-775 and cml_fuzz.rs:557-657 provide boundary and anti-vacuity coverage. This reviewer did not execute tests because the metadata-only contract forbids build artifacts. The separate risk:critical human approval gate remains required.

data.reason: Risk assessment note records no actionable finding.

LGTM for the exact persisted range 40e9dd16..d2672c3d. The prior HIGH type-tree reattachment finding is fixed, all review threads are resolved, and no additional security blocker remains. Static Seal approval does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human gate.
